blocks.content: This topic goes past the Architecture module's overview into kubelet's actual internal loop, the syncLoop, and PLEG, the specific mechanism it uses to notice what the container runtime is actually doing.

At its core, kubelet runs a continuous internal loop, the syncLoop, reconciling the Pods assigned to its node against what is actually running, exactly the general control loop pattern covered earlier in this module, applied specifically at the node level.

blocks.alt: The general control loop pattern, applied specifically at kubelet's own, node-scoped level

blocks.content: The Pod Lifecycle Event Generator (PLEG) is the specific mechanism kubelet uses to notice changes in the container runtime's actual state, container started, stopped, or crashed, without having to constantly, expensively poll the entire runtime state from scratch.

blocks.alt: An efficient, dedicated mechanism for noticing real changes in the container runtime

blocks.content: This is worth being precise about, the liveness, readiness, and startup probes covered in the Health Checks module do not run as part of the same syncLoop tick, each runs on its own independent timer, configured by that probe's own periodSeconds.

blocks.alt: Independent timers, not tied to the same cycle as everything else kubelet does

blocks.content: 4. Status Reporting Has a Real Lag
blocks.text: 4. Status Reporting Has a Real Lag

blocks.content: This is a genuinely practical detail, kubelet does not report a Pod's status back to the API server the instant something changes, it reports periodically, meaning there is always a small, real window where the API server's view can lag slightly behind actual reality on the node.

blocks.alt: A real, small window where the API server's view can genuinely lag behind reality

blocks.content: Kubelet watches the API server for Pods assigned to its node, reconciles that against what PLEG and its probes actually observe, and periodically reports the resulting status back, the complete internal loop underlying everything kubelet does, covered throughout this course.

blocks.alt: The complete internal loop, tying every piece covered so far into one coherent picture

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: kubelet's syncLoop reconciles assigned Pods against reality, using PLEG to efficiently notice container runtime changes without constant, expensive polling.
Probes run on their own independent timers, and status reporting back to the API server has a real, periodic lag, not an instant, real-time update.
